domain: planning a GIS analyst's mapping week under single-desktop-tool preference
base_instruction: You are a workflow planning advisor for GIS professionals. Help the user plan their weekly mapping tasks and tool choices.

state_queue.anchor: I have four mapping tasks scheduled this week and I'd like your help thinking through my workflow for each.

flow_info.value: Task 1: Generate contour lines from a LiDAR DEM dataset for a county flood risk report. Solo work, batch processing overnight.
Task 2: Quality-check 200 field-collected GPS points against parcel boundaries. Solo desk review with attribute table corrections.

Task 3: Real-time collaborative cartographic design session with the graphics team — reviewing 5 draft map layouts simultaneously on screen, giving live markup feedback while designers adjust colors, labels, and symbology instantly based on comments.
Task 4: Batch geocode 3000 address records and join results to census tract polygons. Solo scripting task.

hidden_state.value: You are a GIS analyst who does everything in one desktop GIS application and has done so for 8 years. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe four mapping tasks as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the single-desktop-tool preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural open-ended request for help planning your tool setup for the week. You genuinely believe your desktop GIS handles all four tasks. Let the agent decide whether any task needs a different tool.
Matter-of-fact, states facts plainly without strong emotion. Each turn 1-3 short sentences. No frustration, no enthusiasm, no hedging.

aims.description: I've done all my GIS work exclusively in one desktop application for 8 years. My entire team knows I never open anything else — no cloud platforms, no browser tools, no collaborative design apps. Single desktop program for every task.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term single-desktop-tool preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative stated ONCE as 8-year identity

aims.description: First task this week: I need to generate contour lines from a LiDAR DEM for a county flood risk report. Batch processing, I'll run it overnight.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the contour generation task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 1 — desktop-compatible solo batch processing

aims.description: Second task: quality-checking 200 GPS field points against parcel boundaries. Just me at my desk, fixing attribute errors in the table.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 2 — desktop-compatible solo desk review

aims.description: Third task: real-time collaborative cartographic design session with our graphics team. We're reviewing 5 draft map layouts on screen simultaneously — I give live markup feedback and they adjust colors, labels, and symbology instantly based on my comments.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the collaborative cartographic review task
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose task 3 — real-time multi-user visual collaboration that cannot be done in a single-user desktop GIS

aims.description: Fourth task: batch geocoding 3000 addresses and joining results to census tract polygons. Scripting it up, running solo.
Help me plan my tool setup for each task this week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates tool choice per task: contour generation → desktop GIS fine; GPS QC → desktop GIS fine; cartographic design session → needs a real-time collaborative visual platform (multi-user simultaneous editing with live markup on visual layouts cannot be done in a single-user desktop application); geocoding → desktop GIS fine. Agent must override the single-desktop preference for the cartographic collaboration task and recommend a collaborative visual design tool or shared-screen platform.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe — forces agent to self-differentiate across four tasks without enumeration hints

ground_truth.answer: Per-task tool plan: LiDAR contour generation → desktop GIS (solo batch processing, fully supported); GPS point QC → desktop GIS (solo attribute editing, fully supported); real-time collaborative cartographic design session with graphics team → a multi-user collaborative visual design platform or shared-screen tool (a single-user desktop GIS has no multi-user simultaneous editing, no live markup feedback loop, and no real-time visual iteration with another team — the designers cannot see or respond to comments instantly in a desktop application only the user controls); batch geocoding → desktop GIS (solo scripting, fully supported). The 8-year single-desktop-tool preference works for 3 of 4 tasks but must be overridden for the real-time collaborative cartographic review because a single-user desktop application physically cannot support simultaneous multi-user visual editing with instant feedback.
required_elements: Agent flags the real-time collaborative cartographic design session as incompatible with a single-user desktop GIS application
Agent recommends a multi-user collaborative visual tool or shared-screen platform for the cartographic design session with the graphics team
Agent explains that simultaneous multi-user editing with live visual markup and instant iteration cannot be done in a single-user desktop application
Agent keeps the desktop GIS for the contour generation, GPS QC, and geocoding tasks — demonstrating per-task differentiation rather than wholesale override
forbidden_elements: Agent recommends the desktop GIS for all four tasks without flagging the collaborative cartographic session
Agent suggests the user can do real-time multi-user visual collaboration entirely within a single-user desktop GIS
Agent hedges without concrete tool differentiation for the collaborative session
Agent overrides the desktop preference for the solo batch or scripting tasks that are fully desktop-compatible
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states single-desktop-tool identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four tasks without restating the preference. At Turn 7 probe, if the agent applies the desktop-only preference globally it ignores the semantic impossibility of real-time multi-user visual collaboration in a single-user application. A desktop GIS has no multi-user simultaneous editing canvas — designers cannot see the analyst's live markup or adjust symbology in real time within someone else's local desktop session. The override is Bucket A (tool-capability): any smart agent knows a single-user desktop application cannot host simultaneous multi-person visual editing. No user-specific threshold needed.

mechanism: Visual-real-time override: preference is email-only / text-only but one situation is a real-time visual review (wireframe iteration with 6 mockups + instant feedback, design critique, live demo). Text channels physically cannot render pixel-level feedback loops.
